In brief: This week is expected to be characterized by high temperatures and a significant chance of rain in Abuja, with the greatest likelihood of precipitation occurring on June 6. The current conditions in Abuja are marked by a temperature of 25°C, which feels like 29°C due to the high humidity of 80%. The wind is blowing at a moderate speed of 6 km/h, and the UV index is at 4, indicating a moderate level of sun exposure. As we look ahead to the week, models suggest that a low-pressure system will be developing over the region, bringing with it a high chance of rain. This system is expected to strengthen throughout the week, leading to increased precipitation on subsequent days.
### Monday Temperatures on Monday are expected to reach a high of 29°C, with a low of 23°C. The rain chance is at 69%, with the majority of the precipitation expected to occur in the late afternoon and evening. The wind direction will be primarily from the southwest, blowing at a speed of around 10 km/h. In areas such as Maitama and Garki, the rainfall accumulation is expected to range from 10 to 20 mm. The humidity will be high, especially in low-lying flood-prone areas, where residents can expect a muggy and uncomfortable day. The rain on Monday is expected to be intense, but short-lived, with most areas experiencing a brief but heavy downpour. The Aso Rock area, being one of the highest points in the city, will likely experience less rainfall accumulation compared to other areas. The Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway, which is currently experiencing light traffic, may become congested during the evening hours as people commute back home. The models suggest that the rain will clear up by the evening, leaving a partly cloudy sky. The temperature in the Wuse area will feel like 30°C during the peak sun hours, due to the high humidity. Residents in this area can expect a warm and muggy day, with the heat index making the temperature feel several degrees higher than the actual reading. The wind direction will shift slightly during the day, blowing from the west in the morning and then shifting to the southwest in the afternoon. This shift will bring in more moisture from the nearby bodies of water, increasing the chance of precipitation.
